_comment: A plugin is a provider the user has an account with, not a category. Its settings live here once and reach every app that ticks it. The fields are never repeated here: they belong to the skill's setup.json, which is also what the build's own question uses, so the two can never drift apart. Several choices with the same id are modes of one plugin - Stripe test and Stripe live ask for the same three keys, so they are one card with a switch and not two cards that overwrite each other.

plugins.name: Stripe
plugins.what: Card payments, subscriptions and refunds, most places in the world.

modes.label: Test mode
modes.hint: No real money moves. Start here.

modes.label: Real payments
modes.hint: Live keys. Real cards are charged.

plugins.name: PayHere
plugins.what: Cards, bank transfers and wallets in Sri Lanka, in rupees.

modes.label: Sandbox
modes.hint: No real money moves.

modes.label: Real payments
modes.hint: Live merchant account.

plugins.name: Resend
plugins.what: Transactional email — confirmations, receipts, password resets.

modes.label: Their sender
modes.hint: Sends from onboarding@resend.dev. Nothing to verify, but it only reaches you.

modes.label: Your own domain
modes.hint: Sends as you. The domain has to be verified in Resend first.

plugins.name: Twilio
plugins.what: SMS — one-time codes, reminders, delivery alerts.

modes.label: SMS
modes.hint: A Twilio number that can send to your country.

plugins.name: Supabase
plugins.what: A storage bucket with public URLs. The same project can hold a database.
plugins._no_signin: Deliberate. `supabase login` hands back an account access token, which is not what this plugin needs: the fields are the project URL, its service_role key and a bucket name, and getting those from the CLI is login, then projects list, then api-keys for whichever ref the person picks. A four-step flow with a choice in the middle is not the one-command-one-credential shape vercel and netlify have, so it is its own piece of work rather than a line in this file.

modes.label: Storage bucket
modes.hint: Create the bucket first — the app will not.

plugins.name: Cloudinary
plugins.what: Stores the file and resizes it on the way out, in one service.

modes.label: Store and resize
modes.hint: Nothing else to set up.

plugins.name: ImageBoss
plugins.what: Resizes from a bucket you already own. Needs the bucket's keys too.

modes.label: Resize from your bucket
modes.hint: ImageBoss holds no files; your S3-compatible bucket does.

plugins.name: Google
plugins.what: Sign in with a Google account instead of a password you store.

modes.label: Sign in with Google
modes.hint: Register the redirect URI in the Google console or sign-in is refused.

plugins.name: PayPal
plugins.what: Recognised almost everywhere, and buyers can pay without a card.

modes.label: PayPal
modes.hint: Set the environment to sandbox until real money should move.

plugins.name: Razorpay
plugins.what: Cards, UPI, netbanking and wallets in India, in rupees.

modes.label: Razorpay
modes.hint: Test keys start rzp_test_, live ones rzp_live_.

plugins.name: SendGrid
plugins.what: High-volume transactional email, with a free tier.

modes.label: Email
modes.hint: The from address has to be a verified sender, or nothing arrives.

plugins.name: Mailgun
plugins.what: Transactional email from your own domain, with EU hosting.

modes.label: Email
modes.hint: The sending domain is the one you verified, not your website's.

plugins.name: Amazon S3
plugins.what: The bucket every other tool understands. Also R2, Spaces, Wasabi and B2.

modes.label: Bucket
modes.hint: Give the endpoint for anything that is not Amazon's own S3.

plugins.name: GitHub
plugins.what: For anything developers use. An account may have no public email.

modes.label: Sign in with GitHub
modes.hint: The callback URL must match the one registered, exactly.

plugins.name: Facebook
plugins.what: Reach outside the developer world, especially on mobile.

modes.label: Sign in with Facebook
modes.hint: The app needs review before it leaves test mode.

plugins.name: Microsoft
plugins.what: Work and school accounts, plus personal ones. What an intranet expects.

modes.label: Sign in with Microsoft
modes.hint: Tenant 'common' accepts any account; your tenant id accepts one organisation.

plugins.name: Google Maps
plugins.what: Maps, place search and turning an address into coordinates.

modes.label: Maps and places
modes.hint: Two keys: one for the browser, restricted by domain, one for the server.

plugins.name: Mapbox
plugins.what: Vector maps you can style yourself, with a generous free tier.

modes.label: Maps and places
modes.hint: pk. goes in the page; sk. is for server-side geocoding only.

plugins.name: Google Analytics
plugins.what: Free, and what most reporting expects. Needs a consent banner in the EU.

modes.label: Measure
modes.hint: The measurement id starts with G-.

plugins.name: PostHog
plugins.what: Product analytics with funnels and session replay. Self-hostable.

modes.label: Measure
modes.hint: Pick the EU host if your data must stay in Europe.

plugins.name: Plausible
plugins.what: No cookies and no personal data, so no consent banner. Paid.

modes.label: Measure
modes.hint: The domain is exactly as you added it, with no https://.
